mappings.note: The grouped-mean assumption that frequencies sit at class marks. Belongs to the mean methods of LO-1; no median or mode content.
Deviation-sum identity behind the direct-method mean formula. LO-1; median and mode are untouched.
Identifies u_i = (x_i - a)/h in the step-deviation formula. LO-1 explicitly fuses direct, assumed-mean and step-deviation, so there is no step-deviation sibling to prefer.
Requires the median class via cumulative frequency AND the modal class via maximum frequency, then adds their lower limits. Both outcomes are load-bearing; neither alone answers it.
Makes inclusive classes continuous, then locates N/2 in the cumulative frequencies. The continuity correction serves the median class, so LO-3 and not LO-2.
Differences a less-than table only to find the maximum ordinary frequency. The target is the modal class, so LO-2 rather than the cumulative-frequency LO-3.
Needs the median class (N/2 = 33.5 falls in 125-145) and the modal class (max frequency 20) separately, even though they coincide here. Both outcomes are exercised.

Counts athletes under 14.6 s, i.e. reads a less-than cumulative frequency, but never reaches a median. LO-3 is the only outcome naming cumulative frequency; no outcome covers building a cumulative table as an end in itself (see defect note).
Recovers a class frequency by differencing a more-than cumulative table. Cumulative-frequency handling, so LO-3; not C-8.2-LO-1 because no curve is drawn or read.
Uses total = mean x count twice to find the tenth weight. Direct-method mean property; no ordering or frequency work.
Assertion-reason on the ((n+1)/2)th rule for odd n; the assertion fails because the 6th ordered value is 27, not 30. Positional median, LO-3.
Computes class marks of two intervals. The class mark is the representative value the mean methods rest on; no outcome covers grouped-table structure on its own.
Solves (n+1)/2 = 15 from the mean of the first n naturals. Mean computation, LO-1.
Names the abscissa of the two ogives' intersection as the median. Graphical median, which is C-8.2-LO-1, not the tabular LO-3.
Empirical relation Mode = 3 Median - 2 Mean used to get the mean. No LO covers the empirical relation and no grouped-mean method is used, so competency level.
Recovers a class limit from mid value and width; class-mark arithmetic, the setup of the direct-mean method.
Selects mode as the measure for the most common garment size. Only mode outcome available.
Rearranges the empirical relation into Mode - Median = 2(Median - Mean). Three-measure relation with no single-measure computation.
Cumulative frequencies then N/2 = 30 gives the median class 160-165. LO-3.
Shifting only the top four of nine observations leaves the 5th, the median, fixed. Positional median reasoning.
Solves for x from a given mean and means a sub-list. Direct-method mean.
Highest-frequency value of a raw list is the mode. LO-2.
Very-short twin of the 10th-student weight item; total = mean x count. Mean only.
b is the median because a < b < c, then the mean supplies a + c. Median is the decisive step, mean secondary.
Solves the mean of squares for n and stops there. Unlike its MCQ twin it never asks for a median, so LO-1 alone.
